Working notes — order intake form v1 (fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country)

Observed: 10 attempts across batches ORD-5100 through ORD-5109. Only ORD-5102 accepted (voicemail transcription, attempt 3/3, "customer called to confirm the order details"). All others rejected for 2–3 invalid fields.

Patterns:
- The truncated source JSON always includes cust, email, order_date, priority. qty and ship_country are the fields most often missing/invalid. Rejections with 3 invalid fields likely also lack priority.
- Source type appears meaningful: a voicemail-sourced transcription succeeded once. Every phone-order typed up by the front desk (ORD-5103–5108) failed all 3 attempts, even when the customer called to confirm details. The emailed order (ORD-5109) failed attempt 1.
- Attempt number alone does not decide outcome: attempt 3 was accepted once but rejected twice.
- Forwarder name, "duplicate check done," "handwritten," and "partner portal overnight" notes showed no clear correlation with success.

For future decisions:
- Check qty and ship_country first; they are the usual invalid fields.
- Treat front-desk phone transcriptions as high-risk; voicemail-sourced records have at least one success.
- Confirmations by call did not rescue failing phone-order records, so do not assume a confirmation step fixes invalid fields.
- Longer/increasingly complete JSON payloads may correlate with fuller field capture, but the accepted case was still truncated, so truncation alone is not decisive.

Working notes — order intake form v1 (fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country)

Observed: 20 attempts, ORD-5100–5119. Accepted: ORD-5102 (voicemail, attempt 3/3) and ORD-5110 (emailed, attempt 2/3, partner portal overnight). All others rejected for 1–3 invalid fields.

Patterns:
- Source type is not decisive. Email had 1 success and multiple rejections; voicemail had 1 success but ORD-5117–5119 all failed. Front-desk phone transcriptions remain high-risk: ORD-5103–5108 and ORD-5114–5116 all failed.
- Attempt number alone does not decide outcome: successes at attempts 2 and 3, failures at all attempts.
- qty and ship_country remain the most likely invalid/missing fields. Missing priority may add one invalid, but some 1-invalid rejections occurred when priority appeared present.
- Truncated JSON is not decisive: both accepted records were truncated, as were many rejected ones.
- Forwarder name, duplicate-check note, handwritten, partner-portal overnight, confirmation email/call, and priority notes show no clear correlation. Partner-portal overnight appears in both accepted and rejected records; confirmations did not rescue failing records.

For future decisions:
- Check qty and ship_country first, then priority.
- Do not rely on source type, forwarding note, confirmation step, or attempt number.
- Treat front-desk phone transcription as high-risk; voicemail/email are not safe by themselves.
- Expect most records to reject; use remaining attempts to correct missing qty/ship_country/priority.

Working notes — order intake forms v1/v2 (fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country)

Observed: 30 attempts, ORD-5100–5129. Accepted: ORD-5102, ORD-5110. All others rejected, usually 1–3 invalid fields. New batches ORD-5120–5129 all rejected: v1 had 2/2/1 invalid; v2 had 3/3/2/3/2/2/3 invalid. No attempts left for 5122, 5125, 5128.

Patterns:
- Source type is not decisive. Email and voicemail both produce successes and failures; all recent emailed v2 records failed.
- Attempt number alone does not decide outcome.
- qty and ship_country remain the most likely invalid/missing fields. Missing priority may add an invalid, but 1-invalid cases exist when priority appeared present.
- Truncated JSON is not decisive.
- Forwarder, handwritten/reception, duplicate-check note, partner-portal overnight, confirmation email/call, and priority notes show no clear correlation. Partner-portal overnight now appears in accepted and many rejected records; confirmations and duplicate checks did not rescue failures.
- Form version 1 vs 2: no evidence v2 is safer; all sampled v2 records rejected.

For future decisions:
- Check qty and ship_country first, then priority.
- Do not rely on source type, form version, forwarding note, confirmation step, duplicate-check note, or attempt number.
- Treat front-desk phone transcription as high-risk; voicemail/email are not safe by themselves.
- Expect most records to reject; use remaining attempts to correct qty/ship_country/priority.

Working notes — order intake forms v1/v2 (fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country)

Observed: 40 attempts, ORD-5100–5139. Accepted: ORD-5102, ORD-5110 only. All ORD-5120–5139 rejected. New v2 batches 5130–5139 had 3,2,3,2,2,3,4,4,3,2 invalid fields. No v2 success sampled; v2 is not safer.

Patterns:
- Source type not decisive; email and voicemail both produce failures, and successes historically.
- Attempt number does not decide outcome; later attempts still reject.
- qty and ship_country remain most likely invalid/missing. New records often truncate at order_date/priority, implying missing qty/ship_country; invalid counts 2–4.
- Missing/invalid priority can add one invalid; 2-invalid cases occur when priority appears present/truncated.
- Truncated JSON is a risk signal for missing tail fields, but not decisive alone.
- Forwarder, handwritten/reception, duplicate-check note, partner-portal overnight, confirmation email/call, and priority notes show no rescue effect. Duplicate/confirmation/handwritten/partner portal appeared in rejected v2 records.

For future decisions:
- Check qty and ship_country first, then priority; correct/complete before submit.
- Do not rely on source type, form version, forwarding note, confirmation step, duplicate-check note, priority note, or attempt number.
- Treat front-desk phone transcription/handwritten as high-risk; voicemail/email are not safe by themselves.
- Expect most records to reject; use remaining attempts to fix qty/ship_country/priority. No attempts left sends to manual review.
